The different elements of the story work together seamlessly to create a unified psychological portrait of postpartum disorientation and ambivalence. The surreal, dreamlike nighttime encounters in the maternity ward—where other women are confused about time, identity, and which babies belong to whom—directly mirror and set up Mara's own internal conflict. This builds logically to the climax, where Mara convinces herself she has brought home the "wrong" baby, an illusion that paradoxically allows her to finally feel joy and bond with her child. Every scene, from the opening loss of language to the final acceptance of the baby, serves the central theme of navigating the overwhelming transition into motherhood.
